discovery: Metal halide perovskites as efficient photovoltaic absorbers and the invention of the solid-state perovskite solar cell
subfield: Condensed matter and materials physics / photovoltaics
motivation: In 2009 Miyasaka showed that lead halide perovskites act as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells. In 2012 Park and Snaith, working independently, turned them into solid-state devices, and Snaith showed that the perovskite itself carries charge over long distances, so the mesoporous scaffold is not needed. This established a new class of semiconductors that can be processed from solution. They have strong absorption, tolerance to defects, long carrier diffusion lengths and bandgaps that can be tuned by composition. Physics that had been seen as possible only in carefully grown crystals turned out to work in low-temperature thin films. In just over a decade, certified efficiencies have risen from about 10% to more than 26%, and perovskite–silicon tandems have passed 33%, which is beyond the single-junction limit of silicon. Perovskites are now being commercialised for solar energy and are opening up LEDs and radiation detectors. This is a discovery of great benefit to humanity, as Nobel intended.
